captions.instagram:
What are waves and resonance?

Shake a rope, pluck a string, switch on a microwave: it's the same rule every time, speed = frequency × wavelength. Play with waves on a rope, in air and in light, push a swing and a washing machine into resonance, and find out what really brought down the Tacoma Narrows Bridge.

→ A wave carries a shape and energy along a rope, while the rope itself only moves up and down.
→ Pull it tighter and the wave speeds up, so each wavelength stretches: λ = v ÷ f.
→ Sound is air squeezed and stretched, a pressure wave racing out at 343 metres a second.
→ A string pinned at both ends only rings where whole half-waves fit: fₙ = n × v ÷ 2L.
→ A microwave oven’s 12 cm waves bounce into a standing wave with hot spots 6 cm apart.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/waveclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: What are waves and resonance? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Shake a rope, pluck a string, switch on a microwave: it's the same rule every time, speed = frequency × wavelength. Play with waves on a rope, in air and in light, push a swing and a washing machine into resonance, and find out what really brought down the Tacoma Narrows Bridge.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/waveclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/waveclear

In this video:
• A wave carries energy, not stuff. Shake a rope and a shape runs along it while each bit of rope only goes up and down.
• Sound is squeezed air. A loudspeaker pushes air into bunches that race away at 343 m/s.
• Light is a wave too. Radio, microwaves, light and X-rays are electromagnetic waves, all at c.
• Resonance: push in step. Everything that can wobble has a natural frequency.
• Surprises and a myth. Waves add, so they can cancel: calm lines between ripples, beats between close notes.
